```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(here)

# Created by R/01-clean-data.R and R/02-analysis.R: run those first
results <- readRDS(here("output", "results.rds"))
study <- results$study
gaps <- results$gaps
sleep_row <- results$gpa_table |> filter(term == "sleep_hours")
stress_row <- results$dropout_table |> filter(term == "stress")
support_row <- results$dropout_table |> filter(term == "support")

format_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < .001" else paste("p =", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Participants

The sample included `r nrow(study)` graduate students, `r sum(study$programme == "Master's")` in Master's and `r sum(study$programme == "PhD")` in doctoral programmes (@tbl-sample).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of the sample."
tibble::tibble(
  Characteristic = c("Age, mean (SD)", "Women", "Part-time",
                     "Stress (1-5), mean (SD)", "Wellbeing in semester 1, mean (SD)"),
  Value = c(mean_sd(study$age), percent(study$gender == "Female"),
            percent(study$study_mode == "Part-time"), mean_sd(study$stress),
            mean_sd(study$wellbeing))
) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

## The wellbeing workshop

Wellbeing was similar in the two groups before the workshop (difference `r sprintf("%.1f", gaps$gap[1])` points). After the workshop, invited students' wellbeing was `r sprintf("%.1f", gaps$gap[2])` points higher in semester 2, but the difference narrowed to `r sprintf("%.1f", gaps$gap[3])` points in semester 3 and `r sprintf("%.1f", gaps$gap[4])` in semester 4 (@fig-results, panel A).

![(A) Predicted wellbeing by semester and workshop group. (B) First-semester GPA against hours of sleep.](output/figure-1.png){#fig-results fig-alt="Two panels: wellbeing by semester for the two workshop groups, and GPA against sleep with a regression line."}

## Grade point average

Each additional hour of sleep was associated with a GPA `r sprintf("%.2f", sleep_row$estimate)` points higher (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", sleep_row$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", sleep_row$conf.high)`, `r format_p(sleep_row$p.value)`), holding study hours, stress, and support constant. The model explained `r round(100 * results$gpa_fit$r.squared)`% of the variation in first-semester GPA.

## Considering dropping out

Each one-point increase in stress was associated with `r sprintf("%.1f", stress_row$estimate)` times the odds of considering dropping out (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f", stress_row$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", stress_row$conf.high)`), and each one-point increase in supervisor support with `r sprintf("%.2f", support_row$estimate)` times the odds (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", support_row$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", support_row$conf.high)`). Effect sizes are interpreted following @cohen1988.
